data.name: Ziggurat 3D Chess
data.detailed_description:
Ziggurat Three Dimensional Chess(TM), is a true three dimensional environment which combine the familiar movements of standard chess and exciting new moves never seen before. The rules of movement are easy to learn so beginners will be playing their first game in minutes. Along with the standard board, which is the lowest level of the Ziggurat and the chess pieces on it, there are seven additional levels and twenty five additional pieces to move. While the standard pieces stay on the lowest level, like ground forces in a real war, the additional pieces have unique moves that can take them to new squares on the same or different levels - up or down! Some stay only on even or odd levels while others move between all of them. The Wizard is the most powerful piece with dramatic reach in many different directions - like a super Queen! Falcons move in jumps between levels, between and through other pieces similar to knights, while Paladins are knights - but able to move in L-steps up and down as well as across! The other new pieces: Guards, Ballistas and Cardinals also have their own unique moves through the Ziggurat game board. Watch the videos to get an idea of how these pieces move. But one thing stays the same in Ziggurat 3D Chess - to win you must checkmate your opponents king!
The ultimate challenge of Ziggurat is greater than chess, because there are more pieces, more squares and more ways to move.

data.legal_notice: Ziggurat 3D chess and the Ziggurat logo are trademarked by Lampel Enterprises. The Ziggurat game board is U.S. patent #388,129. The rules for Ziggurat 3D Chess and the piece names for the Guard, Falcon, Ballista, Cardinal, Wizard, and Paladin are copyrighted.

reviews.review: The project functions as a free-to-play, multi-layered strategy matrix and spatial board game sandbox, successfully attempting to reconstruct traditional chess logic within a patented three-dimensional architecture.Stylistically, the software introduces a complex mathematical extension to classic abstraction: the transition from a flat 8x8 layout into an 8-level ziggurat canvas yields deep structural scale. The integration of 25 specialized asymmetrical assets—such as the multi-level leaping Falcon, the spatial L-stepping Paladin, and the hyper-flexible Wizard—successfully transforms traditional positioning into a complex vertical battlefield, generating intense immediate engagement for avant-garde abstract strategy enthusiasts.Mechanically, the interactive core relies on strict multi-dimensional geometric logic: user agency is expanded by distinct altitude-shifting rulesets where pieces move up or down across odd and even levels to execute checkmate conditions. While the tactical depth is highly ambitious, the overall software execution suffers from an archaic, unrefined visual presentation that heavily compromises spatial ergonomics and pieces clarity across different altitude thresholds. Additionally, the lack of automated online matchmaking infrastructure isolates the operator within localized shared-screen loops or simplistic AI routines.Ultimately, this is a highly cerebral digital artifact with restricted long-term player retention. It offers frictionless, cost-free utility for specialized chess theorists investigating multi-dimensional rule-set mutations, providing a unique patented interface that delivers distinct logical challenges despite its outdated visual framework.
